options.title: Shut the Strait of Hormuz. Then what?
options.first_line: Shut the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow gap of sea between Iran and Oman, for one week. Who feels it first?
options.first_frame: The Gulf on the old map, a giant red gate already swinging shut across the strait, tankers bunching up behind it.

options.title: Hormuz shuts for a week. Who runs out first?
options.first_line: The Strait of Hormuz shuts for a week. Which country runs out first?
options.first_frame: A day counter sign reading DAY ONE planted on the strait between Iran and Oman, a red barrier dropping across the water.

options.title: Every Gulf tanker squeezes through Hormuz. What if it shut?
options.first_line: Every tanker leaving the Gulf squeezes through one gap: the Strait of Hormuz. What if it shut?
options.first_frame: Seen from above, a single file of tankers threading the narrow strait between Iran and Oman, the name HORMUZ writing on across the water.

why: It names the place and asks one concrete question (which country runs out first) that only the end can answer, in the shortest line, and the DAY ONE counter with a barrier dropping tells the stakes even on mute.
